scanner.metaTitle: WuWa Translator OCR — Solaris-3 Alphabet Decoder
scanner.metaDesc: Scan Wuthering Waves screenshots and translate the Solaris-3 alphabet with an ONNX model that runs 100% in your browser. WuWa Font Scanner and manual translator.
scanner.hero.body: Upload a screenshot, paste with Ctrl+V or use a sample image. A lightweight CNN detector (ONNX) runs in your browser: crop, boost the contrast and read the transcription without uploading anything to any server.

scanner.how.1b: Fit the frame around the line or the sign. A clean crop dramatically improves small-glyph detection.

scanner.faq.label: Resonance archive
scanner.faq.title: OCR frequently asked questions
scanner.faq.1q: What is the Solaris-3 alphabet of Wuthering Waves?
scanner.faq.1a: It is the fictional writing system Kuro Games uses on signs, menus and panels in Wuthering Waves. It is a substitution of the Latin alphabet: every English letter gets a different glyph, so it can be translated letter by letter.
scanner.faq.2q: Why are the period and the letter A the same class?
scanner.faq.2a: The official font draws 'A', 'a' and '.' with exactly the same outline. Training two visually identical classes would make the network fail. The detector uses a single class and post-processing decides it is a period when the glyph appears isolated at the end of a word or sentence.
scanner.faq.3q: Are my screenshots uploaded to a server?
scanner.faq.3a: No. The ONNX model is downloaded once and runs with ONNX Runtime Web (WASM) inside your browser. Cropping, pre-processing and inference all happen on your device.
scanner.faq.4q: Does it work with lowercase letters?
scanner.faq.4a: Yes, implicitly. In Solaris-3 Script lowercase letters share the same glyph as uppercase, so the 26 A-Z classes cover both cases. The transcription is shown in uppercase.

manual.metaDesc: Type text and convert it to the Solaris-3 alphabet of Wuthering Waves in real time, or build the translation glyph by glyph with the visual keyboard. Copy the text or download a PNG.
manual.title: Solaris-3 manual translator
manual.body: Type in English and watch the Solaris-3 version appear instantly. You can also build the translation glyph by glyph with the visual keyboard and download the result as a PNG image to share it.
manual.editHint: You can type directly here: the glyph is drawn with the official font.
manual.placeholder: Type here to see the translation…
manual.noteBody: The glyph for A is identical to the period .; that is why detection merges them into one class and uses context to tell them apart. The available brackets are [ ]: the font has no braces.
manual.keyboardHint: Click to add the glyph to the text.
manual.reverseBody: if the OCR fails on a hard letter, compare your screenshot glyph with this grid and click the matching symbol to build the translation by hand.

alphabet.metaTitle: Full Solaris-3 alphabet — WuWa Font Scanner
alphabet.metaDesc: Complete table of the 45 glyphs of the Solaris-3 alphabet from Wuthering Waves: letters A-Z, digits 0-9 and signs. Includes a live converter and notes about the period and the brackets.
alphabet.body: 45 unique glyphs: 26 letters, 10 digits and 9 punctuation marks. Lowercase letters share the same drawing as uppercase, so they are not trained as separate classes.
alphabet.lettersNote: A – Z. The glyph is shown as the font draws it; the equivalent Latin letter appears below.
alphabet.digitsNote: 0 – 9. They have their own calligraphic style, different from the letters.
alphabet.punctNote: Parentheses, comma, hyphen, slash, colon, semicolon and brackets. The font has no braces { }.
alphabet.note1t: A and period are the same glyph
alphabet.note1b: The font draws A, a and . with the same outline. The detector uses a single class; post-processing decides it is a period when it appears isolated at the end of a word or line.
alphabet.note2b: The symbols available after Z are [ and ]. Braces are not part of the repertoire of Solaris-3 Script.ttf.
alphabet.note3b: The alphabet is unicase: it does not distinguish uppercase from lowercase. That is why the OCR returns the transcription in uppercase and only 26 letter classes are trained.
alphabet.posterTitle: The table that started it all
alphabet.posterBody: Visual reference of the alphabet with the Latin equivalents. Use it together with the manual translator's visual keyboard to check difficult or ambiguous glyphs.
alphabet.posterAlt: Solaris-3 alphabet poster with Latin equivalents
variants.metaTitle: Other lore variants — WuWa Translator OCR
variants.metaDesc: Lahairoi, Raguna and other regional calligraphies from Wuthering Waves. Shown as lore reference only; they are not part of the Solaris-3 alphabet supported by the OCR.
variants.body: Wuthering Waves includes other cursive writing systems used in different regions. This page shows them only as cultural reference: the detector and translator of this project are trained only with the standard Solaris-3 alphabet.
variants.warnBody: The Lahairoi, Raguna and beta samples were not used to build the dataset or to validate the model. Mixing them would contaminate training: their cursive strokes and ligatures do not match the discrete Solaris-3 glyphs.
variants.supportedBody: If your screenshot uses the discrete glyphs from in-game signs and menus, the scanner should work. Check the full table to compare each symbol before scanning.
variants.cardNote: Unicase, Latin substitution, brackets instead of braces and the period merged with A.
